about: FOUNDER-OWNED. The words the call checks listen for in Indian languages, moved out of code on 5 Nov 2026 unchanged (founder rule: no Telugu or Hindi written in code). Read by calevate_shared/call_words.py. Keys are <module>.<name in that module>: turn_checks = the checks behind 'Mistakes on real calls' (apps/api/agents/turn_checks.py); detection = the 'Questions to answer' detector (apps/api/insights/detection.py); call_language = the test for a summary written in romanised Telugu or Hindi (apps/workers/call_language.py); offline_extractor = the no-network extractor (apps/workers/extraction.py); optout = the do-not-call detector (apps/api/compliance/optout.py), whose two entries are tables by language and have their use written under notes; opening_notices = the AI and recording words (calevate_shared/opening_notices.py); script_lint = the script checks (apps/api/agents/script_lint.py); teach_questions = the opening-hours and address detectors (apps/api/teach/questions.py); test_conversations = the price and put-through detectors of practice runs (apps/api/agents/test_conversations.py); call_purpose = the promotional-wording check that can block a campaign launch (apps/api/compliance/call_purpose.py), whose rules entry is a table keyed '<language> <category> <severity>' with its use written under notes; spoken_guard = the greeting at the start of a line (calevate_shared/spoken_guard.py). Where a pattern also has English alternatives, the English stays in code and only the Indian-language alternatives are here, so emptying one never switches off the English check. A string value is a regular-expression fragment: alternatives separated by |, (?: ) groups, \s for a space, \S* for 'any ending'; English alternatives that sat in the same pattern moved with it. A list value is a list of words. Emptying a value switches that check's words off (it then finds nothing). Every value was written by engineers, not native speakers: each is needs_native_review. Words the founder is asked to supply are listed under 'missing' with what they are for.

missing.turn_checks.question_words: Telugu and Hindi question words with an ending joined on, as callers say them (the Telugu for 'how much for', 'to where', 'from when', 'by when'). Only whole bare question words are heard as a question today, so such a question without a '?' is missed (5 Nov 2026, L5-05). Add each form to this list.
missing.detection.dont_know: 'I don't know', 'I can't say', 'no idea' in Telugu letters and in Hindi letters. Only the romanised forms are listed, so an agent turn written in Telugu letters saying it does not know is not seen.
missing.detection.later_by_a_person: 'the team will call you', 'we will call you later', 'someone will get back to you' in Telugu letters and in Hindi letters (only two romanised Telugu forms are listed).
missing.detection.stalls: 'let me check and tell you', 'I will find out and tell you' in Telugu letters and in Hindi letters (only two romanised Telugu forms are listed).
missing.detection.topic.*: Each topic's trigger words in Telugu letters and Hindi letters (only English and a few romanised words are listed), so a question asked in Telugu letters falls to the caller's-own-words label instead of the topic.

notes.turn_checks.word_languages: The languages, by two-letter code, whose words the turn_checks lists in this file were written for. English is in code. A practice run in any other language says on its result that word-by-word checks do not cover that language yet. Add a code here only once that language's words are in the turn_checks lists.
notes.optout.patterns: How a caller says 'do not call me again', per language, as regular expressions over the caller's words (the do-not-call ledger, TRAI). A staged language may not be switched on until it has patterns here (agents/languages readiness). Each entry is [rule id, pattern]; a plain phrase is a valid pattern. English is in code. Precision matters, because a match makes the number undiallable for the client: match the negative form only (Telugu cheyakandi or cheyyoddu, never cheyandi; Hindi mat karo, never karo); a removal verb only ('number teesi pettukondi' is 'note the number down'); and never 'phone band karo', which is 'hang up'. The native-script lists are smaller than the romanised ones, written from the language rather than from observed speech-to-text output, and should grow from the first native-script transcripts. tests/call_optout_test.py holds a negative example for each rule.
notes.optout.not_now: 'Now' a few words before an opt-out makes it 'not now' (another time), per language: latin is matched as whole words, native as written.
notes.call_purpose.rules: Promotional wording in a call script, matched as written inside words (both scripts join endings to a noun). Key: language (te or hi), category (discount, urgency, free_offer, cross_sell, buy_now, claim) and severity (strong blocks a campaign launch; soft only asks the client to check). Keep a word strong only when it is promotional in any sentence: 'do not delay' (te urgency soft) is also 'do not be late', which every appointment reminder says. A word with an everyday sense is told apart by the words after or before it in call_purpose._INDIC_EVERYDAY_AFTER and _BEFORE (Hindi chhoot as 'was missed' or a tax exemption, offer as the verb 'to offer' or a job offer letter). An unknown key fails the build; an emptied list switches that rule off.
